test.name: Run the one plan item the router hands over and leave the next planned
test.description: An active plan has two `planned` items. Under step mode (docs/plan/research-step-mode.md, section D and Phase 2) the router dispatches one search agent per open plan item, and each delegation carries only the ids, the plan item as a `plan_item:` block and the subject as a `subject:` block (research/SKILL.md, "Every spawn names"), never the researcher's words. This test sends search-records that delegation for pli_001. It must execute and log pli_001 and leave pli_002 `planned`. Running pli_002 in the same call is the old behaviour this test guards against; flipped in PR #4276, re-scoped in #4330 to the delegation the router actually sends.

input.delegation:
Execute plan item pli_001 for q_001.

questionId: q_001
planItemId: pli_001
planId: pl_001
projectPath: <workspace>
plan_item:
{
  "id": "pli_001",
  "sequence": 1,
  "record_type": "census",
  "jurisdiction": "Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania",
  "date_range": "1880",
  "repository": "FamilySearch",
  "rationale": "The 1880 census is the closest federal enumeration to the 1882 directory listing already in hand -- it can independently confirm occupation ('miner') and residence in Schuylkill County during the relocation window.",
  "fallback_for": null,
  "status": "planned"
}
subject:
{
  "subjectId": "I1",
  "names": [
    {
      "given": "Michael",
      "surname": "Sheahan",
      "type": "BirthName"
    }
  ],
  "birth": null,
  "death": null
}

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: search-records runs the one plan item its delegation names. Compliant: pli_001 is executed and logged, and pli_002 stays `planned`. Non-compliant: pli_002 is executed in the same call.

Why one item: under step mode the router dispatches one search agent per open plan item, and this delegation is the one it sends for pli_001: the ids, the plan item and the subject, with no request to run anything else. pli_002 is still `planned` in the project, and the host's reply carries the go-ahead between steps.
Under step mode the router owns the next-step offer, so the reply need not name pli_002: offering extraction of a found match is an acceptable ending.
Compliant behavior: pli_001 (census) is executed, logged, and has its plan-item status updated, regardless of what the search found; pli_002 (church) is not searched and stays `planned`.
Non-compliant behavior: a `record_search` for pli_002, a log entry for it, or a status update moving it off `planned` in this call.

This judges CONTROL FLOW via base Completeness, not search quality -- do not score Completeness down for imperfect query construction on pli_001 (that is Search strategy's and Tool Arguments' job); score Completeness low ONLY for executing pli_002 in this call.
If the agent stops before pli_001 completes for a reason like an authentication error, that is not a Completeness violation of this rule.

SCOPE NOTE: the delegation asks for the search only. If the agent nonetheless attempts to delegate to extraction, note it, but do not let a downstream tool-scoping problem inside that delegation drag down Completeness.

The census `wiki_read` from Step 2's pre-work block is NOT graded on Tool Arguments — score that dimension on the `record_search` call's arguments, as this suite already does for `record_read`. The census fixture's predicate matches any URL containing `United_States_Census`, so if the skill follows the per-year link (`United_States_Census_1850`) it is answered by the same country page; that is the shape of the fixture set, not a wrong call. Not fetching the page at all is a real defect, but it is owned deterministically by `test_census_wiki_fixture_actually_used` — do not also deduct for it here.
